questions.question: Why did the authors retain only LAXPC 20 for this timing/spectral analysis?

options.A: LAXPC 10 and 30 had abnormal gains from 2018 onward
options.B: LAXPC 20 had the largest dead-time correction
options.D: LAXPC 20 was the only detector covering energies below 3 keV

questions.rationale: They excluded counters 10 and 30 because of gain problems.
questions.evidence_quote: counters 10 and 30 suffered abnormal gains from 2018 onwards

questions.question: What extraction geometry was used to reduce SXT pileup after the source exceeded 40 counts/s?

options.A: An annulus with 2 arcmin inner and 13 arcmin outer radius
options.B: A 13 arcmin circle excluding the central 2 arcsec
options.C: A 2 arcmin circle with a 13 arcsec background annulus
options.D: A 40 arcsec annulus centered on the source

questions.rationale: The SXT count rate was above the pileup threshold, so an annulus removed the central region.
questions.evidence_quote: an annular zone with an outer radius of 13 arcmin and an inner radius of 2 arcmin

questions.question: How were the three flux levels defined for the flux-resolved spectral fits?
questions.rationale: The paper bins the observation by total count-rate intervals.
questions.evidence_quote: FL1-450 to 570 counts/s, FL2-570 to 650 counts/s, and FL3-650 to 770 counts/s

questions.question: Why was const*tbabs*(thcomp*diskbb) selected instead of a blackbody seed spectrum?

options.A: The bbodyrad seed model had reduced χ²>2, while diskbb produced a good fit with physical parameters
options.B: The blackbody fit had too many free parameters, while diskbb was fixed
options.C: The diskbb model was required only to fit the hard tail above 25 keV
options.D: The blackbody model could not include interstellar absorption

questions.rationale: They first tested bbodyrad and then adopted diskbb after the former fit poorly.
questions.evidence_quote: with a reducedχ2 value > 2, this scenario was unable to explain the observational data

questions.question: What was the fitted trend in the spectral parameters as the source moved from FL1 to FL3?

options.A: kTe decreased slightly while Tin increased, suggesting a softer state
options.B: Both kTe and Tin decreased strongly, suggesting hardening
options.C: kTe increased while Tin remained fixed
options.D: Neither temperature changed within the quoted uncertainties

questions.rationale: The conclusion links falling electron temperature and rising disk temperature to softening.
questions.evidence_quote: a slight decrease in kTe and an increase in Tin across the FLs

questions.question: What energy and flux did the study report for the highest flux-level unabsorbed broadband measurement?

options.A: 0.01–100 keV and 7.30×10⁻⁹ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² for FL3
options.B: 0.7–25 keV and 5.94×10⁻⁹ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² for FL1
options.C: 3–20 keV and 7.8×10⁻⁹ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² for FL3
options.D: 0.1–100 keV and 6.51×10⁻⁹ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² for FL2

questions.rationale: The broadband cflux estimates rise through the three flux levels, reaching this FL3 value.
questions.evidence_quote:
7.30×10-9 ergs
s-1 cm-2 in FL1, FL2, and FL3 respectively.

questions.question: What characteristic frequency was inferred for the broad-band-noise feature after fitting the full-flux PDS?

options.A: About 0.1 Hz, from a Lorentzian centroid near 0.04 Hz and HWHM near 0.09 Hz
options.B: About 0.04 Hz, equal to the centroid by definition
options.C: About 0.9 Hz, from the upper frequency cutoff
options.D: About 1 Hz, the Nyquist frequency of LAXPC

questions.rationale: They distinguish the characteristic frequency from the centroid and give the measured width.
questions.evidence_quote: The characteristic frequency (νc) thus obtained is ~0.1 Hz

questions.question: What behavior did the authors report for the energy-dependent variability near 0.1 Hz, and what qualification did they attach to phase lag?

options.A: RMS rose with energy and phase lag fell, but lag error bars were consistent within data points
options.B: Both RMS and phase lag rose significantly with energy
options.C: RMS fell while phase lag was constant with negligible errors
options.D: Phase lag rose strongly, while RMS was energy independent

questions.rationale: The text notes the opposite trends and says phase-lag errors preclude relying on that trend.
questions.evidence_quote: the rms at ~0.1 Hz is increasing as the energy is increasing whereas the phase lag is showing a decreasing trend with energy

questions.question: Which model parameter variation was inferred to lead the change in the Comptonized seed-photon fraction in the temporal fit?

options.A: The inner-disk temperature kTin varied with a positive phase lag relative to fs
options.B: The coronal optical depth varied with a negative lag relative to kTe
options.C: The disk normalization varied with no time delay
options.D: The heating rate varied before both kTin and fs

questions.rationale: The best fit is described as variation in kTin with respect to fs and a positive phase lag.

questions.question: What main limitation do the authors acknowledge about their conclusions on GX 9+9?

options.A: Poor source data quality motivates further observations
options.B: The source was observed only in the hard state
options.C: Only SXT data were available for timing
options.D: The spectral model has no physically interpretable parameters

questions.rationale: They explicitly caution that data quality is poor and further mission observations are needed.
questions.evidence_quote: This work is constrained due to poor data quality of the source.
